synthesis: Convolution first rewrites the target analytic observable in coefficient form while keeping the missing singular data explicit: for zeta this is a Fourier-filtered Dirichlet series plus a pole residue, and for log zeta it is a von-Mangoldt series plus a correction from zeros to the right of the line. Under RH the latter correction vanishes at the ranges used for S and S1. When the kernel weights make the resulting Dirichlet coefficients nonnegative and absolutely summable, the resonance mean expands into nonnegative terms, so one may retain only a finite subcollection aligned with the resonator's approximate multiplicative relations; restricting the von-Mangoldt series to the prepared prime band then recovers the divisor statistic built into the resonator.
source_support: Unit w2609909332_zeta_convolution_identity proves the zeta convolution identity by contour shifting and separates the Fourier-weighted coefficients from the pole residue. Unit w2609909332_log_convolution_zero_correction gives the log-zeta prime series and explicit off-line-zero correction, then derives the RH-conditional S and S1 formulas. Unit w2609909332_positive_dirichlet_resonance_lemma expands an absolutely convergent nonnegative Dirichlet series against the resonator and discards all but a favorable finite subcollection. Unit w2609909332_von_mangoldt_resonance_lemma restricts the analogous series to selected primes, where Lambda(p)/log p=1, and invokes the prepared divisor-mass lemma to obtain the stated gain.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes two distinct representation choices: smoothing exposes coefficient data while isolating pole or zero information that a bare Dirichlet series omits, and positivity turns the resulting analytic mean into a monotone selector of multiplicative correlations. The prime restriction then aligns those correlations with the exact coordinates used in the resonator construction.
limits: The zeta convolution is unconditional under its kernel hypotheses, but removing the zero correction in the log-zeta, S, and S1 formulas is conditional on RH. Positivity and absolute convergence are essential; the resonance lemmas do not apply directly to signed or conditionally convergent series and cannot symmetrically select negative real parts. A material continuation of Lemma 6 is imported from earlier work. The pole residue has conflicting-looking signs or kernel arguments in the extracted statement and proof, and Fourier conventions, zero sums, coefficient minima, radicals, errors, and logarithmic scales are OCR-sensitive. These identities and lower-bound mechanisms imply neither RH nor a general smoothing principle for arbitrary observables.
quality_reason: Accepted because the four parents jointly support a concrete smooth-to-coefficients-to-positive-selection pipeline, with the pole and zero corrections, RH boundary, and sign obstruction retained rather than polished away.

synthesis: The resonator is designed by balancing three separate resources. Square-free weights on logarithmic prime bands create a large multiplicative divisor statistic. Occupancy caps remove over- and under-populated band configurations so that the retained divisor-closed set has cardinality at most N, while exponential tilting shows that the exceptional weighted mass is negligible. Finally, geometric cells of relative width about 1/T replace each occupied cell by one representative and aggregate nearby squared weights; in the Gaussian Fourier expansion, rapid decay suppresses separated cells, while a Cauchy-Schwarz comparison transfers exact relations in the original support to approximate relations among the representatives.
source_support: Unit w2609909332_prime_band_resonator_construction defines the square-free prime-band weights, removes excessive occupancies, retains divisor closure, and states the cardinality bound. Unit w2609909332_weighted_mass_survives_truncation introduces a narrower typical set and uses bandwise Euler products plus a tilt with negative exponent to show exceptional f-squared mass is negligible and to prove the weighted divisor-statistic lower bound. Unit w2609909332_geometric_thinning_controls_off_diagonal defines the cell representatives and aggregated coefficients, proves the Gaussian-smoothed L2 bound by diagonal/off-diagonal separation, and gives inequality (21) transferring exact multiplicative relations to a 3/T tolerance after thinning.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis links combinatorial concentration to Fourier geometry: band occupancy controls how much multiplicative structure fits in the support, tilting certifies that this capacity restriction preserves the useful weighted statistic, and geometric thinning compresses it at exactly the log-frequency resolution seen by a length-T Gaussian mean.
limits: The construction and parameter balance are specific to the chosen prime range, square-free weights, logarithmic target scale, and Gaussian resolution. Lemma 3 and parts of the tail estimates are imported from earlier work rather than reproved here. The thinning preserves multiplicative relations only within the stated tolerance, and Lemma 5 controls resonator normalization rather than proving correlation with a target series. Prime-window endpoints, f(p), occupancy thresholds, set operations, tilt exponents, Euler factors, cell endpoints, coefficient neighborhoods, and constants are extraction-sensitive. This is not an automatic template for arbitrary signed coefficients, kernels, or scales, and it does not characterize an optimal resonator.
quality_reason: Accepted because the three parents jointly certify gain, finite capacity, preservation of the weighted mass, and Fourier-compatible compression. Each proof burden remains separate and source bounded.

synthesis: Kernel parity determines both which component of the conditional log-zeta formula is exposed and which sign conclusion resonance can preserve. For S, a real odd differentiated Gaussian has a purely imaginary Fourier transform; its prime-band imaginary weights can be made positive for Lemma 7, but the physical-side kernel changes sign, so the argument controls only a large absolute value of S. For S1, a real even Gaussian is nonnegative and has a positive real Fourier transform; after the extra logarithmic attenuation in the S1 coefficients, the same resonance mechanism preserves order and yields a one-sided positive extreme.
source_support: Unit w2609909332_log_convolution_zero_correction derives, under RH, the imaginary prime-series formula for S and the real prime-series formula for S1, the latter with an extra logarithmic denominator and a bounded correction. Unit w2609909332_odd_kernel_selects_s chooses the odd differentiated Gaussian, verifies the imaginary Fourier weights on the prime band, localizes the mean, and obtains max |S| via Lemma 7. Unit w2609909332_even_kernel_selects_s1 chooses the positive even Gaussian, uses the real S1 formula and the lower bound for K-hat(log p)/log p, and derives a positive maximum.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis compares two complete proof chains and identifies parity as a joint observable-and-order selector: oddness rotates the frequency weights into the imaginary component but sacrifices physical-side order, whereas even nonnegativity retains the real component and one-sided order. The added log denominator explains the distinct S1 coefficient scale without conflating the two observables.
limits: Both S and S1 convolution applications are conditional on RH and do not supply evidence for it. The S result is only an absolute extreme and identifies neither sign nor prevalence; the S1 result proves only a positive extreme and gives no negative counterpart. The bounded h correction is absorbed as an error but does not make S1 identical to the integrated log modulus. Kernel normalizations, Fourier phases, coefficient minima, error placement, extra parentheses, and final iterated-log powers are OCR-sensitive. The mechanism explains the asymmetry of these proofs, not the true sign distribution or optimal order of S or S1.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three parents jointly support the parity-to-component-to-sign mechanism, and the synthesis preserves RH conditionality and the different logical strength of absolute versus one-sided conclusions.

synthesis: The authors attribute the improved detectable amplitude to a resonator using larger primes and a longer Dirichlet polynomial than earlier resonance work, but explicitly record two costs: the interval on which existence is obtained is considerably larger than in predecessor results, and no comparable estimate is known for the measure of the large-value set. In the zeta proof, a compact-frequency nonnegative kernel exposes a positive coefficient block, while second-moment localization, Gaussian tail decay, and the budget kappa<1-beta control the enlarged time range; the proof then gives existence of a large value and adjusts parameters back to the theorem's stated interval, not a prevalence statement.
source_support: Unit w2609909332_resonance_tradeoffs_and_sign_obstruction explicitly compares the longer, larger-prime resonator with Soundararajan's earlier resonator, states the gain in maxima together with larger intervals and the missing measure estimate, and labels suggested measure adaptations as unproved. Unit w2609909332_theorem1_kernel_and_localization gives the sinc-squared/triangular Fourier filter, removes the central and far ranges, imposes kappa<1-beta, applies the convolution and positive resonance lemmas, locates one large value first on an enlarged interval, and then rescales to the theorem range.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis connects the paper's methodological comparison to the actual localization ledger in the proof: resonator length supports a larger coefficient construction, while central-range removal, far-tail decay, and the kappa-versus-beta constraint determine where the resulting existential maximum can be certified. This separates amplitude, localization, and prevalence as different outputs.
limits: The proof establishes existence of at least one large value, not the measure or frequency of such values. The suggested adaptation of prior measure results and the hoped-for stronger theorem are mentioned without proof, and quantitative comparisons with cited predecessors are not independently auditable in this packet. The proof initially works on an enlarged interval and depends on a final rescaling; this does not establish that the interval loss is optimal or unavoidable. Kernel scaling, triangular Fourier normalization, pole residue, error exponents, interval endpoints, and nested-log gains are formula-sensitive, and the residue inherits the sign/argument ambiguity of Lemma 1. No optimal-order, typical-value, or zero-distribution conclusion follows.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two parents jointly support both the qualitative tradeoff and its concrete proof-level localization costs, while unproved prevalence adaptations and any optimality reading remain explicitly outside the conclusion.
